text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Diagnose ME/CFS by clinical criteria after exclusion tests, explain that it is a real illness with no diagnostic test, and give her a written care and support plan, including a flare plan
  • Energy management led by the patient: an activity and symptom diary, planned rest before and between tasks, work broken into short blocks, and heart-rate awareness; no graded exercise therapy or fixed increases in activity
  • Infectious diseases consultation to look for relapsed or focal brucellosis or another persisting infection before attributing her symptoms to ME/CFS
  • Orthostatic intolerance measures: 2 to 2.5 L of fluid a day, more salt with meals, waist-high compression garments, and tasks done seated or reclined; repeat the standing test at six months
  • Sleep, pain, and cognitive symptom care: a regular sleep window with rest periods kept short, acetaminophen as needed, no sedatives or opioids, and memory aids for work
  • Vitamin D repletion with cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily, rechecked after about three months
  • Review the care plan at every visit, with PHQ-9, PROMIS fatigue and physical function scores, and a pain score; primary care review at least yearly and more often while the plan is new
  • Workplace adjustments: home working, a reclined workstation, flexible hours, and meetings by video or at her home

resource.title: Florence Nightingale synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognize post-infectious myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in a 37-year-old nurse administrator and statistician, make the diagnosis by clinical criteria after a focused set of exclusion tests (including a reasoned decision about past brucellosis), and manage it by NICE NG206 and CDC guidance: energy management and pacing without graded exercise therapy, orthostatic intolerance measures, sleep and pain care, mood screening, function scales, and workplace adjustments that protect the productive working life that matters most to her.
